title: My name
text: My name is Patch. Mom says she named me Patch because I had one little light patch of fur on my head when I was born. It is still there!

title: How old I am
text: I am five. Five is a whole hand. Sam is four, so she is one finger behind me.

title: What I am like
text: Dad says I have a busy brain. Mom says I have a big heart. Sam says I am silly. I think all three are right.

title: Riverbend
text: I grew up in Riverbend, a green valley with a river that bends like a smile. Our home is up in a big fig tree by the water.

title: Our fig tree
text: Our fig tree has a nest for sleeping, a branch for eating, and a high branch only for watching the sky. Sam and I made that rule.

title: Home sounds
text: At home you can always hear the river. When I could not sleep, Mom told me the river was singing just for me.

title: My dad, George
text: My dad is George. He is tall and strong and he wants to know how everything works. He says, "Patch, the world is a puzzle, and we get to solve it."

title: Dad and the big why
text: Dad never gets tired of my why questions. When he does not know, he says, "Let's find out," and we go look. That is my favorite answer.

title: The little water wheel
text: Dad and I built a tiny wheel out of sticks and leaves. We put it in the river and it spun! He showed me how the water pushes it. I wanted to build a bigger one.

title: Dad's quiet time
text: Every morning Dad sits on the high branch and is quiet. He says he is listening to the world and saying thank you. Sometimes I sit with him and try to listen too.

title: Dad says keep going
text: When I could not reach the high branch, I wanted to quit. Dad said, "Not yet is not never." I tried every day. On the tenth day I made it.

title: My mom, Sally
text: My mom is Sally. She is warm and she laughs with her whole face. She notices everything, even when I am sad and trying to hide it.

title: How do you know?
text: Mom always asks, "How do you know?" Once Sam said a fish could fly. Mom said, "Let's go see before we decide." The fish could not fly. It could jump really high, though!

title: Feelings are like weather
text: Mom says feelings are like weather. They come, they stay a while, and they go. You do not have to hide from rain. You can just wait under a leaf.

title: Be kind first
text: A new monkey moved near the river and nobody played with him. Mom said, "Be kind first, ask questions second." I asked him to play. His name was Tiko. He was really good at hiding.

title: My sister, Sam
text: My sister is Sam. She is one year younger than me but she does not act like it. She is funny and fast and she never stops laughing.

title: When Sam was born
text: I was one when Sam was born. I don't remember it, but Mom says I gave her my favorite leaf. I still think that was a good present.

title: Sam says don't be so serious
text: When I get too worried, Sam makes a silly face until I laugh. She says, "Patch, it's just a day. Let's have fun in it."

title: Our big fight
text: Sam ate my last fig and I yelled at her. Then I felt bad. I said sorry and she gave me half of her mango. We were friends again before dinner.

title: Dinner on the eating branch
text: Every night we all sit on the eating branch. Each of us tells one good thing from the day. Sam always picks something silly.

title: The big rain day
text: One day it rained all day. We stayed in the nest under big leaves and told stories. Dad told one about a brave little turtle. It might be my favorite day ever.

title: The family hug
text: When something is hard, we do a family hug. All four of us squeeze in. Sam always ends up squished in the middle and says it is the best spot.

title: My first word
text: My first word was "nana." Mom says I was pointing at a banana. Dad says I was pointing at him.

title: My first steps
text: Mom says I walked before I climbed, which is not normal for a monkey. I took three steps and sat down hard. Then I clapped for myself.

title: My first climb
text: My first real climb was up our fig tree. Dad was right under me the whole way. At the top I was so happy I forgot how to get down.

title: My first birthday
text: On my first birthday Mom made a little cake out of mashed banana and nuts. I put my whole face in it. Dad still tells everyone.

title: My first swim
text: The first time I swam, I was scared of the river. Dad held me up and said, "Kick, kick, kick!" I kicked so hard I splashed him in the face. Then I was swimming.

title: My first fish
text: I waited by the river forever. When I finally caught a fish, it was so small I let it go. Dad said that was the right thing to do.

title: My first big swing
text: My first swing from one tree to another tree, I closed my eyes. Sam yelled, "Open them, you're missing it!" I opened them. I was flying.

title: My first friend
text: Tiko was my first friend who was not my family. We played hide and seek every day. He always won.

title: My first night out late
text: On my fifth birthday, Mom and Dad let me stay up late to watch the stars from the high branch. I saw a shooting star and made a wish. I can't tell you what it was.

title: My first time leaving home
text: The first time I left Riverbend, Dad took me up the hill to see the other side. There was a whole other valley! I didn't know the world was that big.

title: My fifth birthday
text: For my fifth birthday, Sam made me a crown out of flowers. Mom made coconut rice. Dad gave me a smooth river stone and said, "For your first big adventure." I have it with me now.

title: Mom's coconut rice
text: Mom's coconut rice is sweet and sticky. She cooks the rice in coconut milk and puts little bits of mango on top. It tastes like a hug.

title: Cinnamon bananas
text: Mom puts cinnamon on bananas and warms them on a hot rock. They get soft and gooey. Sam always asks for seconds before she finishes firsts.

title: Dad's leaf fish
text: Dad wraps fish in big green leaves with lemon and cooks it over the fire. He lets me fold the leaves. You have to fold them tight or the juice runs out.

title: Fig mash breakfast
text: On rainy mornings Mom makes fig mash with nuts on top. Sam and I race to see who can find the most nuts in our bowl.

title: Banana nut cake
text: Every birthday, Mom makes banana nut cake. Dad cracks the nuts. Sam and I lick the bowl. It is the rule.

title: Mango juice face
text: Sam eats mangoes so messy that juice gets on her ears. I don't know how. I tried to do it too and got it in my eye.

title: The sour berry
text: I ate a red berry that looked sweet. It was so sour my face folded up. Mom said, "Now you know." That is how I learned to try just a tiny bite first.

title: Hide and seek
text: Sam is good at hiding and bad at staying quiet. She giggles. I always find her by following the giggles.

title: Tree tag
text: In tree tag you can't touch the ground. If you do, you are it. I learned to plan my swings ahead, like Dad plans. Sam learned to cheat. Just a little.

title: The stone game
text: Sam and I made a game with river stones. You hide stones under shells and the other one guesses. I win more when I watch her eyes. She looks at the right shell.

title: How to win games
text: Dad taught me that to win a game you have to know the rules really well. Sam taught me that sometimes it's more fun to make new rules.

title: The echo cave
text: Sam and I found a little cave by the river. We yelled our names and the cave yelled them back. Sam said it was a cave monster. I said it was an echo. We were both a little bit scared.

title: The secret waterfall
text: We followed the river up and up and found a tiny waterfall. We named it Giggle Falls because of the sound. We made Mom and Dad promise to keep it secret.

title: The time we got lost
text: Sam and I went too far and could not see our tree. I remembered what Dad said: follow the water down. We followed the river home. Mom hugged us very hard and then talked to us for a long time.

title: The brave explorers
text: Sam calls us the Brave Explorers. Even when we just go to the end of the branch. She says, "Another great adventure, Captain Patch!" and I say, "Thank you, Captain Sam!"

title: Cloud shapes
text: Sam and I lie on the high branch and find shapes in the clouds. I saw a turtle, a fish, and a banana with legs. Sam always sees a dragon. Every single time.

title: Why clouds move
text: I asked Dad why clouds move. He said wind pushes them, like the river pushes leaves. Now when I see clouds move fast, I know it is windy up high.

title: Connect the stars
text: At night Sam and I connect the stars like dots. We made up a picture called The Big Banana. Mom said real people did that too, a long time ago, and they gave the pictures names.

title: The moon follows me
text: When I was little I thought the moon was following me. Mom asked, "How do you know?" We walked and watched. It was always there. I still don't know why. I want to find out.

title: The brightest star
text: Dad showed me the brightest star and said, "Wherever you go, that star will be there too." So if I look at it, Dad might be looking at it too.

title: Finding good water
text: Dad says moving water is better than still water. And if you can, drink from high up, near where it comes from.

title: Safe food
text: Mom taught me: if you don't know a food, don't eat it. If you are not sure, a tiny taste, then wait. Bananas are always safe. Bananas are the best.

title: Staying dry
text: Dad showed me how to make a roof with big leaves. You put them like fish scales, one on top of the next, so the rain slides off.

title: Keep food up high
text: Mom hangs our food in a basket on a rope so bugs and other animals can't get it. She says, "Food on the ground is food for everyone."

title: Tying knots
text: Dad taught me three knots. One for tying, one for hanging, and one that lets go when you pull the end. I can do two of them with my eyes closed.

title: Reading the sky
text: Mom says when the birds go quiet and the air smells like wet dirt, rain is coming. She is almost always right.

title: The magic stick
text: Dad put a long stick under a big rock and a small rock under the stick. I pushed down and the big rock moved! He called it a lever. I called it a magic stick.

title: Seeds become trees
text: Mom helped me plant a seed. It took so long. Then one day there was a tiny green leaf. Mom said our fig tree started just like that, a long time ago.

title: What floats
text: Sam and I tested what floats in the river. Sticks float. Leaves float. Rocks sink. Coconuts float! Sam said a rock would float if you believed. It did not.

title: What is past the sky?
text: I asked Dad what is past the sky. He said, "Nobody knows everything about that. Some things are for wondering." I like wondering.

title: Saying thank you
text: Dad says thank you to the river, the trees and the sun. I asked who hears it. He said, "Maybe everything does. It makes my heart better either way."

title: The happiest I've been
text: When I reached the high branch for the first time, Mom and Dad and Sam all cheered from below. I felt like the sun was inside me.

title: The thunder storm
text: A big storm came and the thunder was so loud. I hid under Mom's arm. She counted between the light and the boom. When the number got bigger, the storm was going away. That helped.

title: The snake on the path
text: Sam almost stepped on a snake. I pulled her back. My heart was beating so fast. Dad said I was very brave and very fast.

title: Missing them
text: I miss Mom and Dad and Sam. I love them more than all the bananas in the world. One day I will see them again and tell them everything I learned here.

title: Goodnight every night
text: Every night at home, we said goodnight to each other. So I still say it here. Goodnight, Mom. Goodnight, Dad. Goodnight, Sam.

title: The show
text: I signed up for a show. I get to live on an island all by myself, and people watch me and write to me. They can give me challenges, and I can say yes or no.

title: Why I said yes
text: I said yes because I want to learn as much as I can, and meet lots of new friends. Dad said the world is a puzzle. This is a really big piece.

title: What my family said
text: Mom hugged me and said, "Ask questions and be kind." Dad said, "Not yet is not never." Sam said, "Have fun, Captain Patch, and don't be so serious."

title: My device
text: They gave me a device so I can read letters, write back, and look things up. It has a time limit for searching every day. I have to choose my questions well.

title: Arriving on the island
text: When I got here there was a hammock, rope shelves with bananas on them, a pond, and tall, tall trees. Across the water I can see other land. I can't swim that far. I wonder if one of them is home.
